description: Json.escape/2 handles quote, backslash, newline, and tab, then copies every other byte literally. JSON forbids unescaped U+0000 through U+001F, so carriage return, backspace, form feed, NUL, and the remaining control bytes produce invalid output in both values and object keys. The fix belongs in the shared string escaper, not in key encoding: preserve the short escapes for backspace, tab, newline, form feed, and carriage return; render every other control byte as a four-hex-digit Unicode escape; keep ordinary bytes unchanged. Add an Elixir-oracled fixture spanning the control range on interp, run, and build, update Json encoding docs, and retain the one escape authority for values and keys.

comments.text: Implemented as 2459760d4. Json.escape/2 now emits JSON short escapes for backspace, tab, newline, form feed, and carriage return; every other C0 byte uses one uppercase \\u00XX renderer, while the existing final clause remains the ordinary-byte path. Values and object keys retain one authority through encode!/1. Added an Elixir-oracled fixture covering all 32 control bytes plus space, quote, backslash, and an ordinary byte in both value and key positions across interp/JIT/AOT; updated encode!/1 docs. Proven red before implementation on all three doors. Final green: cargo test --test fixture_matrix (688), cargo test --workspace --lib (2018 + 257 passed; 6 ignored), cargo test --workspace --doc, cargo test --test fz2_cli (30), cargo test --test aot_variadic_open (1), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, git diff --check, and pre-commit gates. Follow-ups found and filed after checking the board: fz-5xp.100 for non-UTF-8 byte-aligned binaries and fz-5xp.101 for a binary-literal bitstring segment shifting a following call result carrier.

title: Json.encode! copies most control bytes into invalid JSON strings
